one_liner: Supabase offers documented management and data APIs and an official MCP server.

auth.notes: OAuth2 is for third-party integrations acting on users' behalf. The memo says personal access tokens authenticate Management API requests and project API keys authenticate data requests.

access.notes: The most accessible path is a free hosted project with project API keys available in its Dashboard. Self-hosting is another route, but it does not include the Management API. The free-credentials finding relies on the documented availability of free projects and separate key-retrieval documentation.

api.notes: The public Management API covers organizations and projects; project data APIs support database CRUD.

mcp.notes: Supabase documents a hosted MCP connection and available tools. The memo reports that the feature page labels the server General Availability.

verdict.rationale: Free hosted projects provide a path to project API keys, and OAuth2 is documented for third-party Management API integrations. The APIs cover project management and database CRUD, though the Management API is unavailable when self-hosting.

evidence.quote: OAuth2: OAuth2 allows your application to generate tokens on behalf of a Supabase user, providing secure and limited access to their account without requiring their credentials. Use this if you're building a third-party app that needs to create or manage Supabase projects on behalf of your users.
An API key authenticates an application component to give it access to Supabase services. An application component might be a web page, a mobile app, or a server.

problems: I did not find a single complete sentence explicitly tying API-key creation to the Free plan. The access finding relies on the documented availability of free projects plus the documented way to retrieve a project's keys.
The MCP feature page's General Availability designation appears as a label, not a complete sentence; the quoted sentences establish that the official server is usable.
name: Supabase

verification.note: OAuth2 is explicitly recommended for third-party apps managing projects on users' behalf, and API keys are documented for application components, so primary oauth2 is proven. No quote mentions bearer tokens or personal access tokens; that extra listed method is unevidenced but does not overturn the field.

Two active free projects plus publishable keys shown ready to use prove a free hosted path to credentials with no quoted payment, trial, or approval. The self-hosting quote supports deployment_model both and correctly limits the Management API to the managed platform; it does not say self-hosting itself requires payment.

Documented /rest/v1/ routes accepting GET, POST, PATCH, and DELETE, plus a reflected GraphQL API, prove rest and graphql. Org/project management and database CRUD are not described as read-only, so breadth broad is not contradicted. The cited pages are publicly quoted, supporting public_docs and the docs URL.

Supabase's own pages call it the official MCP server and describe connecting and using it now, which supports official and generally_available. No quote uses the words General Availability, but nothing calls it beta, a pilot, or unlaunched.
The Composio toolkit docs page describes a Supabase toolkit, so in_catalog yes is proven.

Self-serve free projects yield API keys and the documented REST/GraphQL and management APIs are broad enough to use, so buildable_now with main_blocker none follows. The self-hosting Management API gap is a caveat in the rationale, not a blocker.
